fieldMarks: Very large, stocky bear without the brown bear's shoulder hump.
Relatively small head and elongated neck.
Fur appears white but can look yellowish in summer or brown/grey depending on light; skin is black.
Males 300-800 kg and up to 2.5 m long; females 150-300 kg.
behavior: Solitary except females with cubs and mating pairs; bears may gather to scavenge a seal kill.
Mainly still-hunts ringed seals at breathing holes, or stalks seals basking on ice; often eats only the blubber.
Strong swimmer that ranges widely; has been documented as far south as Maine.
Uses a 'chuffing' sound as a greeting; has a keen sense of smell.
habitat: Pack ice of the Arctic Ocean, especially ice edges and pressure ridges; in summer on islands, coasts with landfast ice or stranded on land. Pregnant females den on coasts in winter.
range: Circumpolar Arctic. In North America, populations occur in western and northern Alaska and the Canadian Arctic archipelago, following the pack ice south in winter.
